cards.headline: Russian drone strike on emergency workers in Zaporizhzhia region kills at least 55 people

pages.text: A Russian drone strike targeting emergency workers in the village of Komyshuvakha, near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region of southern Ukraine, killed at least 55 people, according to Ukrainian authorities. The drone hit a former school and a nearby shelter that had previously been struck by multiple Russian guided bombs while residents were waiting for humanitarian aid. While a subsequent strike on the same location did not injure anyone, it damaged specialized rescue equipment, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. Ukraine has routinely accused Russia of conducting multiple strikes at the same site in quick succession to target emergency crews responding to initial attacks. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack on the rescue workers as “absolute cynicism and brutality.”

The scale of the casualties in Komyshuvakha remains uncertain as recovery efforts continue. Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, HUR, reported that approximately 50 people were listed as missing, while Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of the regional military administration, stated as of the afternoon that 45 people were listed as missing. Many of the recovered bodies have not been identified, and DNA analysis is ongoing. On November 7, 2026, village resident Mykola Krasnov, 72, reported he was still searching for his wife after she went to receive humanitarian aid, noting that a 3-ton bomb was dropped at the site and she had not been located in the morgue or at home. Another resident, Yurii Karapetian, said his wife Natalia was killed while distributing bread to people in the shelter.

On November 7, 2026, a farewell ceremony was held in Zaporizhzhia for six police officers killed in the Russian strikes on Komyshuvakha, including four who died near the former school. Police lieutenant colonel Andrii Khomenko said the victims used every skill available to protect themselves, but noted that no skills could help when the enemy deliberately gathered civilians in one place before launching strikes. The community also held services for three residents among the dead. In a separate overnight attack, Ukrainian authorities reported that one person was killed and eight were wounded. President Zelenskyy stated that Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles during that attack, which hit energy facilities and a major bridge in the Kyiv region.

cards.headline: At least seven people killed and more than 100 injured in Egypt train collision

pages.text: At least seven people have died and more than 100 have been injured after two trains collided near the Egyptian city of Giza. The collision occurred in the al-Ayyat district, approximately 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo, when one train struck the rear of another service that was stationary on the tracks. The Egyptian National Railways Authority reported that the impact caused several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment. One of the trains involved was traveling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, while the stationary train was heading south from Cairo to Aswan. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those who died. While some reports indicated at least four people were killed and nearly 90 injured, other authorities confirmed at least seven deaths and more than 100 injuries. The public prosecutor's office warned that the death toll could rise.

Emergency responders launched a massive response to the scene, with officials stating that 52 ambulances were deployed. The Egyptian Red Crescent reported providing aid and psychological support to victims and families at the site. Local hospitals were placed on heightened alert to manage the influx of patients, with Health Minister Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar noting that victims are being treated for head injuries and broken bones. Images from the scene showed overturned carriages and uninjured passengers and bystanders searching the wreckage for survivors. To clear the line and restore traffic, cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. As a result, train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region have been suspended.

Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi ordered state authorities to investigate the circumstances of the accident and to hold anyone found to have been negligent accountable. The cause of the accident was not immediately clear. The collision took place in an area that has seen significant rail disasters previously, including a 2002 train fire that killed over 370 people and several crashes in 2009. While Egypt has invested billions of dollars into high-speed rail lines and new highways in recent years, the country continues to face safety issues and repeated crashes as it attempts to revamp its aging rail network, which is the oldest in Africa and the Middle East.

cards.headline: New Zealand election results too close to call as special votes remain uncounted

pages.text: New Zealand faces a potential weeks-long wait to determine the shape of its next government after the 2026 election failed to provide a decisive victory for either the incumbent right-wing coalition or the opposition left bloc. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, leader of the centre-right National party, described the results as “too close to call” on November 7, 2026, noting that special votes must be counted before government negotiations can begin. While National remains the largest party in parliament and maintains a “pathway to forming the next government,” the current seat margins are narrow. Official results are not scheduled for release until 27 November.

On the night of November 7, 2026, with nearly 100% of regular votes counted, the centre-right National party secured 42 seats. National's traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act party and the populist New Zealand First party, secured 13 and 12 seats respectively. This combined 67-seat majority is described as wafer thin, leaving the left bloc just three seats behind. In the party vote, National led the Labour party by 0.02%. Labour, led by Chris Hipkins, secured 35 seats, while its traditional coalition partners, the Greens and Te Pāti Māori (the Māori party), won 16 and five seats respectively.

The uncertainty stems from the pending count of special votes, which include overseas ballots and votes cast outside a voter’s specific electorate. These votes can significantly alter the final seat count; in 2023, approximately 600,000 special votes were made, representing 21% of the total. Historically, these votes have tended to favour the left, such as in 2023 when special votes resulted in the Greens and Te Pāti Māori gaining three seats between them. Because some seats were won by very slim margins, the final composition of parliament remains precarious until the official count is completed.

cards.headline: Bangladesh Election Commission plans five-phase elections for approximately 1,000 union parishads on 21 January

pages.text: The Election Commission (EC) of Bangladesh plans to hold the first phase of elections in approximately 1,000 union parishads (UPs) on 21 January. This is part of a five-phase election programme intended to fill vacancies in local government bodies. The terms of around 4,300 union parishads have already expired, and the EC aims to complete all elections for these bodies by 27 May 2027. Union parishads are the smallest rural administrative units in Bangladesh's local government system. Some UP elections remain pending due to court cases.

EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed disclosed the election plan to journalists at the Election Commission Bhaban in Agargaon on 8 November 2026. Ahmed stated that the second phase is likely to be held on 4 February, while the third, fourth, and fifth phases are scheduled for 29 April, 13 May, and 27 May, respectively. The EC is considering UPs whose terms have expired or are due to expire within the election schedule period. Ahmed noted that elections in all union parishads of an upazila would be held simultaneously if their terms had expired or if they had become eligible for elections.

The EC has almost completed preparations for the first phase, and the lists of UPs for the first and second phases are expected to be finalised soon. The proposed schedule was planned by the EC considering Ramadan, the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations, and weather conditions, particularly in coastal areas.

cards.headline: Six killed and several injured in Krakow shooting

pages.text: A gunman opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second largest city, on November 7, 2026, killing six people and injuring several others. Polish police stated the attacker used military weapons during the shooting in the city's main market square. Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows approximately a dozen people running inside two buildings as a black car with an open front window passes, followed by a police car. Another video captures the moment gunshots were heard in the market square.

Poland's interior minister described the suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, as being inspired by far-right ideologies. Following the attack, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that three other bodies were found at the suspect's home, which remains under search.

cards.headline: At least 34 people killed as small boat sinks off northwestern Senegal

pages.text: At least 34 people have died after a small boat carrying migrants and refugees sank off the coast of northwestern Senegal, according to the Senegalese Press Agency (APS). The Senegalese Interior Ministry reported that one person was rescued, while an indeterminate number of people remain missing. Action for Human Rights and Friendship (ADHA) confirmed the death toll reported by APS. An initial statement from the Senegalese Interior Ministry had provisionally reported 21 bodies and one survivor before the toll was updated to at least 34 by APS. The nationalities of the victims have not been confirmed as search operations continue. Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye stated on Facebook that state authorities and resources have been mobilized to locate missing persons, care for survivors, and support families. The Interior Minister is expected to visit the region to meet with victims' families and express condolences on behalf of the state.

The vessel, a pirogue-type flat-bottomed boat, reportedly capsized on November 7, 2026, off the Loumpoul dunes in the Kebemer department, located between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis. The newspaper Le Soleil reported that most victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts within that department. This tragedy follows a separate incident on November 6, 2026, when Senegalese authorities intercepted 142 migrants on a similar small boat attempting to reach Spain. That group included 23 women, two babies, and two other children from Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Nigeria. The Senegalese Interior Ministry stated it is determined to combat people smuggling networks through strengthened cooperation with neighboring countries.

The sinking occurred along a dangerous Atlantic Ocean route used by thousands of people from West Africa attempting to reach Europe. Migrant rights group Walking Borders reported that 635 people died in the first five months of a recent period. On November 7, 2026, Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro declared an emergency following a surge in migrant boat arrivals. El Hierro authorities stated that since the start of November, more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard approximately 30 boats. Increased maritime patrols by Senegal, Mauritania, and Morocco around departure points have forced boats to head further south toward the coasts of Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea, which prolongs the duration of the hazardous crossing.

cards.headline: US announces Task Force Iron Gate to disrupt Iran’s land and Caspian Sea supply routes

pages.text: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on November 7, 2026, that it is forming Task Force Iron Gate to prevent Iran from using ground routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons and other materials. Based in Tampa, Florida, the unit will reportedly be run by 20 civilian and military personnel. The task force aims to coordinate with other US government agencies to prevent the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper stated the unit will reinforce the existing US blockade of Iranian ports at sea.

The task force expands US efforts to choke Tehran’s military supply networks by targeting land routes and the Caspian Sea, moving beyond the current blockade of Iranian ports. Michael Mulroy, a former US deputy assistant defence secretary for the Middle East, told Al Jazeera that the unit will aim to identify where weapons systems are entering, how they can be cut off, and how Iran is transporting its energy. Mulroy suggested that if US President Donald Trump increases military involvement, there will likely be attacks on a series of targets. He noted that, unlike Operation Epic Fury which focused primarily on military targets, these targets may focus on economic and infrastructure targets as part of a plan to cut the regime off from its ability to fight and fund itself.

The announcement from CENTCOM coincided with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announcing plans for underground complexes designed to sustain missile and drone production during bombardment. These plans follow reports of ongoing construction near Iranian missile bases based on satellite imagery and previous claims by Tehran that US strikes failed to destroy its underground facilities. Iran shares land borders with seven countries: Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan, Turkiye, and Turkmenistan.

cards.headline: Ghana Immigration Service Comptroller-General leads peace talks in Hamile following deadly border clash

pages.text: Samuel Basintale, the Comptroller-General of the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS), has led peace talks with community leaders in Hamile, Upper West Region, to restore calm following a deadly explosion and clashes between residents and security personnel. The engagement aimed to rebuild relations between the community and security agencies after an incident on November 3, 2026, at an unapproved border route known as Mountain Back 2. That incident reportedly involved a tricycle carrying dynamite and resulted in the death of an immigration officer and other persons, while 11 civilians sustained injuries during subsequent confrontations with security personnel. During his visit, Basintale met with immigration personnel, traditional authorities, youth leaders, and representatives of the Hamile Development Committee after receiving a briefing from regional security officials.

Upper West Regional Police Commander DCOP Francis Yiribaare, representing the Regional Security Council chairman, briefed the delegation on the current security situation. Yiribaare stated that nine of the civilians injured during the clashes had been discharged and were scheduled for medical reviews. He noted that a curfew remains in force and security personnel are continuing enforcement, while an integrated security team remains in Hamile to support peace restoration efforts. Although the border has seen a limited reopening, Yiribaare indicated that business activities have not yet fully resumed. Basintale warned that prolonged border closures could worsen congestion and create additional security challenges due to the volume of cargo traffic passing through Hamile, noting that Mali has increasingly relied on the route for cargo transportation. He stated that even a six-hour closure could lead to significant traffic build-up and argued that processing vehicles quickly is preferable to locking the border, as massing crowds between vehicles can become difficult to control.

cards.headline: Russell Brand faces significant prison sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault

pages.text: A London judge is set to hand down a sentence on November 9, 2026, to comedian and actor Russell Brand, who was found guilty of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Following a four-week trial, Judge Joel Bennathan told the 51-year-old Brand that he faces a “significant custodial term.” Brand, a former MTV host who became a Christian and spiritual influencer, had denied all charges and stated he never had sex without consent. After the jury delivered the verdict on November 5, 2026, a judge denied a request from Brand's lawyer to grant bail so Brand could spend the weekend with his three children, resulting in Brand spending the weekend in a London prison cell.

The trial examined seven historic charges brought forward by six different women. Brand was found guilty on four of those charges: one count of rape involving a woman who attended one of his comedy shows in 2009, and three counts of sexual assault occurring between 2004 and 2009. The sexual assaults took place at a bar, a radio station, and a TV studio. Brand was found not guilty of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

While the maximum sentence for rape in the UK is life, crime commentator and former BBC correspondent Danny Shaw noted on X that the average sentence is 10 years. Shaw suggested Brand is likely to receive between four to 13 years of prison time.

cards.headline: One driver dead after tree falls on vehicles in Surrey, B.C.

pages.text: A driver was pronounced dead at the scene after a tree fell across Highway 10 in Surrey, British Columbia, trapping two vehicles around 8 p.m. on November 7, 2026. The Surrey Police Service reported the tree fell between 182 and 184 streets. The driver of the second vehicle involved in the incident suffered minor injuries. Highway 10 was closed overnight but has since reopened to a single lane in each direction.

The fatality occurred as powerful windstorms battered much of the province. Environment Canada recorded wind gusts of up to 90 km/h over Vancouver Island, up to 80 km/h in Prince George, and up to 70 km/h in the Lower Mainland. The storms caused widespread power outages across British Columbia. At the peak of the storm around 1 a.m., approximately 135,000 customers across the province were without electricity. By the morning, more than 63,000 B.C. Hydro customers remained without power, with more than half of those outages located in the Lower Mainland and Sunshine Coast. Hydro identified Surrey, Duncan, Port Hardy, and Prince George as the hardest-hit areas.

cards.headline: Person dies following shooting in Etobicoke

pages.text: A person died after being shot in Etobicoke, according to the Toronto Police Service. Officers responded to the area of Rathburn Road and The East Mall shortly before 4:30 p.m., where they found a person with gunshot wounds. Toronto paramedics confirmed to CBC Toronto that a man had been taken to the hospital in critical condition; Inspector Jeff Allington later told reporters that the victim died at the hospital. Allington stated he did not know the victim's age, but the individual was believed to have been in his teens or his 20s. The homicide unit has taken over the investigation, which Allington described as being in its early stages. Police reported that The East Mall was closed northbound at Rathburn Road for the investigation.

Inspector Jeff Allington, speaking at the scene, provided a description of the suspects, stating they are two male suspects wearing dark clothing. Allington noted that the incident could be traumatic for community members who reside and work in the area.

cards.headline: Ghana found guilty of violating rights of schoolgirls due to menstruation taboo

pages.text: The African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC) ruled on October 20, 2026, that Ghana violated the rights of schoolgirls who are forbidden from crossing the River Offin on Tuesdays and during menstruation. This customary practice forces some girls to miss between seven and twelve school days every month, disrupting their education and academic performance while placing them at a disadvantage compared to boys. The ACERWC, an expert body, adopted the decision during its 48th Ordinary Session in Maseru, Lesotho, following a human rights case brought against Ghana by JoyNews Channel Manager Solomon Joojo Cobbinah and the Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa (IHRDA). The case involved girls living in communities along the River Offin in the Ashanti Region who must cross the river to attend school at Kyekyewere in the Upper Denkyira East Municipality of the Central Region. Under the longstanding customary practice, women and girls are prohibited from crossing the river on Tuesdays and while menstruating due to traditional beliefs that violating the taboo could result in death or danger.

In its ruling, the Committee found that Ghana violated the girls' rights to education and non-discrimination under the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child. The Committee also held that the state failed in its obligation to eliminate harmful social and cultural practices. The decision established that governments cannot avoid responsibility simply because discriminatory practices originate from traditional authorities rather than state institutions. The Committee found that Ghana failed to take adequate measures to address the discriminatory effects of the practice, despite being aware that girls were being denied access to education.

cards.headline: Iran executes three men accused of armed unrest during January protests

pages.text: Iran has executed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zanganeh for roles in armed unrest during anti-government protests in January, according to state media. The state news agency Tasnim reported that the Supreme Court upheld the convictions of the three men, finding them guilty of participating in operational activities on behalf of the United States, the Israeli Zionist regime, and hostile groups. The executions follow a series of deaths linked to the protests, including individuals accused of having ties to Israel and the United States. The number of executions in Iran has increased since US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic began in late February.

The three men were accused of using firearms, bladed weapons, grenades, and Molotov cocktails, as well as setting fire to public facilities in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. Alleged damage included an electricity substation in Karaj that caused power outages in some areas. Hassan Dioband was arrested on 11 January after investigations identified him as a suspect in attacks on public property and incitement to violence. Ten other individuals accused of participating in the unrest under Dioband's supervision were later arrested and, according to Reuters, received prison terms of 5 to 10 years.

The protest movement began in December due to the high cost of living and evolved into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on 8 and 9 of January. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, attributing the violence to terrorist acts orchestrated by Israel and the United States. However, foreign-based NGOs provided higher death figures, and the BBC received multiple accounts from Iranians stating that security forces opened fire on unarmed protesters.

cards.headline: Custom pool ramp provides accessibility for woman with cerebral palsy in Welland, Ontario

pages.text: A woman living with cerebral palsy in Welland, Ontario, can now access her family's backyard pool via a custom-installed ramp. Julie Grand, who requires two canes to walk, previously faced exclusion from outdoor activities due to her disability. When her family decided to build a new backyard pool, they sought a solution that would allow her to enter the water safely and independently without being strapped into a mechanical lift. Most pool companies informed the family that ramps are generally reserved for concrete pools, outdoor city pools, and public facilities like YMCAs. Instead, these companies proposed mechanical lifts that swing and lower a person into the water for a cost of up to $20,000, an option Julie Grand stated she did not want. After Terry Grand, a retired teacher, contacted pool companies in Welland, Hamilton, Windsor, and Toronto, the family connected with Pelham-based Poolbusters, headed by Ryan Kore, to install an accessible ramp in a steel pool with a vinyl liner.

cards.headline: Heavy rain floods approximately 70,000 tents in Gaza

pages.text: Heavy rain from Gaza's first winter storm on November 14, 2026, flooded approximately 70,000 tents within a 12-hour period. The downpour prompted warnings of a worsening humanitarian situation for hundreds of thousands of displaced people living in temporary camps that lack adequate protection from rain and cold. Civil Defense received more than 1,500 distress calls as families fled waterlogged camps overnight, according to Save the Children. In Al-Mawasi, located in southern Gaza’s Khan Younis, a resident named Salma reported that water seeped into her family's tent from above and pooled beneath them despite her layering tarpaulins over the structure to keep out the rain. Basel El-Maqosui, an artist in Gaza City, stated that the sound of raindrops on his family's tent now causes anxiety rather than joy. Many shelters have deteriorated due to prolonged weather exposure and repeated dismantling and rebuilding.

Save the Children reported that more than half a million children in Gaza face their fourth winter in tents or makeshift shelters. The aid group warned that temperatures falling as low as 5 C, combined with restrictions on shelter supplies, are exposing families to potentially deadly conditions. Alexandra Saieh, head of global strategic influencing and policy at Save the Children International, described the situation as a “man-made catastrophe.” Saieh alleged that Israeli authorities have not allowed enough tents through and have prevented recovery and reconstruction by restricting various items. A recent assessment by the Palestine Shelter Cluster, an organization that coordinates the humanitarian shelter response, found that about 1.2 million people—roughly 58 percent of Gaza’s population, including more than 560,000 children—were living in conditions classified as “critical or catastrophic.”

cards.headline: Ghana's Minerals Commission orders major mining companies to transition to contract mining

pages.text: The Minerals Commission, Ghana's mining regulator, has ordered the last three major companies practicing owner-mining to transition to contract mining by December 2026 or face sanctions, including fines and mine shutdowns. Between October 2025 and January 2026, the Commission issued letters to Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti, and Chinese-owned Zijin Mining regarding this directive. This transition is being enforced under the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (L.I.). Under these regulations, surface mining must be handled by wholly Ghanaian-owned firms, while underground mining must go to firms with at least 50% local ownership. This shift from owner-mining—where a company manages its own extraction operations—to contract mining involves outsourcing those operations to local firms. While the Commission aims to increase local control, workers who perform underground mining say they were never consulted about the directive.

cards.headline: Three activists arrested in Berlin after replacing German flag with Palestinian flag

pages.text: Berlin police arrested three activists at the scene after they replaced a German flag with a Palestinian flag outside the German parliament. According to Anadolu Agency citing Berlin police, authorities opened an investigation into the incident on suspicion of insulting the state and its symbols. The group involved, Peacefully Against Genocide, stated the action was intended to show solidarity with Palestinians and to condemn German politicians for failing to act against what the group describes as genocide and grave human rights violations. The group describes itself as a German civil resistance movement that utilizes nonviolent protests, sit-ins, and blockades to oppose military support, arms exports, and what it alleges is German complicity in the war in Gaza and the wider Middle East.

The activists conducted the protest to oppose the German government’s support for Israel and its silence regarding war crimes in Gaza. In a statement, a group member identified only as Aaron accused governments worldwide of failing to represent their people by remaining silent on, permitting, or supporting genocide. Aaron questioned the meaning of the pledge “never again” and the value of international law and human rights if governments do not abide by them or apply them to everyone. Peacefully Against Genocide also announced further protests against Germany’s policy toward Israel and continued arms supplies, calling on arms manufacturer Rheinmetall to halt all deliveries to Israel and close its Berlin facility.

cards.headline: More than 200,000 protesters join Amsterdam ‘Red Line’ demonstration against Israel

pages.text: More than 200,000 people marched through the streets of Amsterdam, Netherlands, to demand government action against Israel’s war in Gaza, according to the Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organizers of the ‘Red Line’ protest. Many participants wore red clothing as they moved through streets closed to traffic. The protesters called for a halt to all arms sales and tighter trade restrictions on Israel. During the march, some participants echoed cries of “Free, free Palestine!” as a man with a loudspeaker shouted the phrase from a bus stop.

The demonstration follows previous ‘Red Line’ protests, including one in The Hague and another in early October. The protesters are responding to Israel’s war in Gaza, which has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including 21,000 children, since October 2023. Although a ceasefire took effect in Gaza on October 10, Israeli attacks and killings have continued on an almost-daily basis since that date. One protester, Mike van Dongen, described the situation in Gaza as inhumane and stated that Dutch authorities are doing nothing and do not dare take any serious steps.

cards.headline: Swecchasebak Dal leader expelled after arrest for allegedly secretly filming women in Barishal

pages.text: Bayezid Mithu, a joint convener of the Uzirpur Municipality Swecchasebak Dal—the volunteer wing of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)—has been expelled from the organization following his arrest in Uzirpur upazila, Barishal. Mithu is accused of secretly filming women in their homes through windows and bathroom ventilators using a mobile phone. Local residents and police reported that Mithu had long been accused of using such recordings to blackmail women and attempt to force them into immoral activities. On the night of November 7, 2026, Mithu was reportedly caught attempting to record a woman's private moments through a bathroom ventilator at approximately 10pm. After the woman noticed him and shouted for help, local residents detained and beat Mithu before handing him over to the Uzirpur Model Police Station. Three eyewitnesses, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that multiple secret videos of women were found on the mobile phone Mithu was carrying at the time of his capture.
Following the incident, police filed a case against Mithu under the Pornography Control Act. On the afternoon of November 8, 2026, a court sent Mithu to jail.

cards.headline: Villagers in Mugla, Turkey demand COP31 leaders inspect coal mining devastation

pages.text: Villagers in Ikizkoy, Turkey, are calling on world leaders attending the COP31 climate talks to visit the Akbelen forest area to witness the impact of decades of lignite extraction. Local official Nejla Isik, an elected representative for her community, stated that government and United Nations officials should travel a few hundred kilometres west from the conference venue in Antalya to inspect how coal mining has affected nature and local lives. Isik's own home is located only a few hundred metres behind a lignite mine that has expanded closer to the community over several decades. Villagers who have protested against coal mining for years have faced arrests and fines. Environmental campaigners and villagers, including Isik, say the expansion of lignite mining has destroyed forests and threatens farmland, olive groves, and local communities. Lignite is the lowest grade of coal, which releases higher amounts of carbon dioxide when burned compared to more energy-dense coal varieties. The mines in the Akbelen area provide coal for plants that generate just over 2% of Turkey's power, according to the operator's website. However, energy think tank Ember reports that coal was Turkey's largest electricity source, generating 34% of the country's power, making Turkey Europe's largest coal-fired electricity generator. The UN conference, which includes the transition to cleaner energy as a theme, is scheduled to begin on November 9, 2026, and continue until November 20 in Antalya on Turkey's Mediterranean coast. One prominent aim of COP31 is to agree on a voluntary goal for increasing electrification, a proposal made by host country Turkey; however, the effectiveness of this goal depends on whether the electricity produced is low-carbon to curb planet-warming emissions.

cards.headline: Scarborough Health Network hosts breast cancer screening event for Black women

pages.text: Dozens of Black women received breast cancer screenings during an awareness event hosted by the Scarborough Health Network at the Northpine Diagnostic Imaging Department. Held in partnership with the Toronto charity The Olive Branch of Hope, the event provided on-site mammograms and educational sessions for eligible women aged 40 to 74. This was the fourth such event held in Scarborough and aimed to provide trusted information to encourage women to take action for their health. Leila Springer, a founder of The Olive Branch of Hope, stated the charity was established 25 years ago to support Black women.

Breast surgeon Winnie Leung, who attended the gathering, reported seeing an increase in breast cancer among younger women over the last four to five years. Leung told CBC Toronto that while her patients were previously typically in their 60s or 70s, with rare cases in their 40s or 50s, the average age is now between 40 and 50. Leung noted that there are currently patients in their 20s and said she would not be surprised if patients began presenting at age 30.

The event follows a policy change in Ontario two years ago when Health Minister Sylvia Jones announced that the mammogram self-referral age was lowered from 50 to 40. Jones described the move as a necessary step because breast cancer affects one in every nine women in the province, noting that early detection can be the difference between life and death. During a mammogram, technologist Michelle Jones explained that four images of the breast tissue are taken, consisting of two views—front and side—for each breast.

cards.headline: Bangladesh’s external debt reaches $113.44 billion, according to World Bank

pages.text: Bangladesh’s external debt has climbed to $113.44 billion, representing a burden of approximately $646 for every citizen, according to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026 released on November 5, 2026. Based on a 2025 population estimate of 175.7 million, the per capita debt is $646, or Tk 80,330 at the prevailing exchange rate. At an exchange rate of Tk 124.35 to the dollar, the total debt amounts to Tk 14.1 trillion. This figure represents an increase from $38.77 billion in 2015, meaning the debt has almost tripled in a decade.

The $113.44 billion total is composed of $89.51 billion in public and publicly guaranteed debt, $9.87 billion in private non-guaranteed debt, and $14.06 billion in short-term debt. Public and publicly guaranteed borrowing includes loans from multilateral institutions and countries, whereas private non-guaranteed debt carries no government backing. Of the public and publicly guaranteed borrowing, multilateral creditors account for $51.14 billion and bilateral lenders account for $32.65 billion. Japan is the largest bilateral creditor with $12.72 billion outstanding, followed by Russia with $9.02 billion, while other countries account for a combined $10.90 billion.

Multilateral lenders hold a significant portion of the public debt. The World Bank is owed $22.64 billion, followed by the Manila-based Asian Development Bank at $17.52 billion. Other multilateral lenders are owed $10.99 billion.

cards.headline: Toronto Pearson and Durham region ER identified as possible measles exposure sites

pages.text: The Durham region health department has confirmed a measles case in an unimmunized child who recently traveled internationally. Health officials are warning that members of the public may have been exposed to the virus at Toronto Pearson airport and an emergency room in the Durham region. Anyone who was in these locations during the specified times of day is asked to monitor for symptoms until Nov. 24, according to a news release from the health department. The department is currently investigating the case and following up directly with individuals known to have been in contact with the child.

Measles is a highly contagious disease that spreads easily to individuals who are not vaccinated and have not previously had the illness. The virus can remain active in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours. Symptoms typically develop between seven and 21 days after infection and include a high fever, cough, runny nose, red watery eyes (conjunctivitis), sensitivity to light, and a red rash that lasts four to seven days. While the health department notes that people born before 1970 would likely have had measles as a child and are protected, children under the age of one, unimmunized pregnant people, and those with weakened immune systems face an increased risk of complications.

Durham region health officials suggest that residents who believe they may have been exposed should confirm they have received two doses of the measles vaccine. If symptoms develop, officials advise individuals to stay home, call ahead before visiting a clinic or primary care centre, and wear a well-fitted mask when seeking a medical assessment.

cards.headline: “Godzilla Minus Zero” sets North American record for foreign-language film debut with $31.6 million

pages.text: “Godzilla Minus Zero” earned $31.6 million over the weekend, setting a record for a foreign-language film debut at the North American box office. Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the film is a sequel to the 2023 Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One.” Produced by Toho and distributed in North America by GKids, the movie is set in post-WWII Japan and returns the franchise to its Japanese roots. This opening surpasses the previous live-action foreign-language record held by 2004’s “Hero,” which launched with $17.9 million. The only live-action foreign-language film to achieve a larger opening weekend was 2004’s “Passion of the Christ,” which opened with $83.8 million despite using largely Aramaic dialogue.

The $31.6 million debut for “Godzilla Minus Zero” outperformed Warner Bros.’ animated film “The Cat in the Hat,” which featured the voice of Bill Hader. According to studio estimates, “The Cat in the Hat” opened with $20.5 million in North America and $10 million overseas. While the “Godzilla” film set a record for live-action foreign-language debuts, the anime “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle” recorded a higher debut of $70.6 million. The weekend also saw the widest North American release for an Indian film.

cards.headline: New extinct megapode species identified from fossil found in Liang Bua cave

pages.text: Researchers have identified a fossilized leg bone as belonging to a new extinct species of megapode, a ground-dwelling, chicken-like bird. The fossil, which is one of the largest of its kind, was discovered in one of the deepest layers of the Liang Bua cave on Flores Island. This discovery represents the first megapode fossil ever found in Wallacea, a transitional zone between Asia and Australia. The study was published in Alcheringa: An Australasian Journal of Palaeontology on November 8, 2026.

The leg bone was originally found by researchers in 2009. At the time, it was identified as a bird bone and set aside, where it remained for approximately 17 years before being identified as this specific new species. The fossil dates to a period between 190,000 and 120,000 years ago. Hanneke Meijer, a professor and curator of osteology at the University Museum of Bergen, noted that the find is one of the oldest bird remains found at Liang Bua and provides data for a period where almost no bird data currently exists.

Megapodes are a group of fowl-like birds that split from other species during the Late Cretaceous. Unlike many birds, megapodes do not sit on their nests; instead, they lay their eggs in large mounds or burrows and leave them. Researchers suggest the group first emerged in Australasia before spreading to parts of eastern Indonesia, Melanesia, the Philippines, and Australia.

cards.headline: JWST identifies more than 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy

pages.text: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have identified 104 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy, located approximately 6.5 billion light-years away. This finding more than doubles the previous record of 44 such detections in the same galaxy. The study, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics in September, provides a rare view of the galaxy's stellar population and may offer hints regarding the nature of dark matter. These magnified events occur due to gravitational lensing, a phenomenon where the gravity of a massive object bends and magnifies light from a more distant source. In this case, the light from the Dragon galaxy is stretched and magnified by a massive galaxy cluster known as Abell 370, with a portion of the galaxy forming a shape called the Dragon arc.

The magnification is not uniform across the galaxy because the Abell 370 cluster is not a uniform mass. Instead, the cluster's gravity bends light by different amounts in different locations. Along specific lines called caustics, the light from the Dragon can be focused so strongly that its brightness increases dramatically. These intense focal points are influenced by the cluster's own stars and potentially by dark matter, which creates small distortions in the lensing effect.

cards.headline: Researchers map rose coral colony stretching 1.56 kilometers in Cocos (Keeling) Islands

pages.text: Researchers have mapped a rose coral (Pachyseris) colony stretching 1.56 kilometers (0.97 miles) along the outer reef of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, making it one of the largest known coral colonies ever recorded. The formation occupies the outer reef slope at depths between 14 and 65 meters (46 and 213 feet). The length of the colony is approximately equivalent to 100 buses parked end to end. The coral has an average width of 36.5 meters (120 feet), covering an area of 56,940 m² (613,000 square feet), with additional sections extending a further 200 to 300 meters (656 to 984 feet) beyond the main colony.

Lead researcher Dr. JP Hobbs from Adelaide University spent months mapping the coral, completing the task over 12 dives. During the process, Dr. Hobbs used GPS to mark progress between dives when running out of air before reaching the end of the formation. While local dive operator Dieter Gerhard first spotted extensive areas of the coral more than 30 years ago, researchers mapping the reef determined the sections may be connected as one enormous colony. The research team included scientists from the Queensland Museum and James Cook University. Researchers are currently using genetic testing to investigate whether the formation is one giant coral organism or multiple colonies that have fused together over time.

cards.headline: Astronomers identify 84 mysterious hypersoft X-ray sources in deep space

pages.text: Astronomers analyzing archival data from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory have identified a new class of cosmic objects known as hypersoft X-ray sources. These objects behave unlike anything previously catalogued and could help resolve long-standing mysteries in astrophysics. Researchers discovered the 84 sources by comparing images taken at different X-ray energies; the objects appeared only in images captured at the lowest energies. The findings were uncovered in data collected by Chandra between 1999 and 2017, and the researchers suggest more may be found in the remaining data. These sources were identified in six galaxies, including the Andromeda and Pinwheel galaxies.

Hypersoft X-ray sources emit unusually low-energy X-rays and intense levels of ultraviolet radiation. Lead researcher Mustafa Muhibullah of the University of Alabama stated, “We’ve never encountered a group of objects that act like this.” Researchers believe these sources may be binary systems, where a compact object—potentially a white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole—pulls material from a companion star. As this material falls toward the compact object, it heats up and produces radiation. The unusual behavior of these sources could help explain Type Ia supernovae, which are used to measure the expansion of the Universe, as the scenarios that trigger such supernovae remain uncertain.

cards.headline: US datacenter demand drives fossil fuel pipeline boom amid deregulation

pages.text: A review of federal records shows that the demand for datacenters is driving a surge in fossil fuel pipeline projects while the Trump administration removes regulations designed to protect natural resources and lives. These pipelines could supply at least 98 gas-fired power plants proposed to serve datacenters. If all the lines are completed, they would transport about 40% more natural gas daily than the amount the system carries on November 8, 2026. Most of the pipelines would carry natural gas across 42 states, with concentrations in fossil fuel-producing regions including 42 in or crossing Texas, 27 in Louisiana, and nine each in Pennsylvania and Illinois. Alexandra Shaykevich, a research manager with the Environmental Integrity Project, described the situation as the largest boom in a couple of decades coinciding with deregulation. Shaykevich noted that while pipelines usually operate safely, they can leak and explode, posing risks to communities across the United States. The US currently records approximately 1.7 pipeline accidents, spills, fires, or explosions per day.

The expansion occurs as the Trump administration reduces protections from foundational environmental laws, such as the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act, which advocates say were previously used to stop risky projects, protect against accidents, or hold polluters accountable. According to the report, over 25% of the pipeline projects have requested an expedited environmental review. The administration is largely using mechanisms such as invoking an “energy emergency” to push these projects through, which the report describes as legally dubious.

cards.headline: Scientists produce record-breaking, ultra-intense 300-attosecond X-ray flashes

pages.text: Researchers have achieved a world record by producing extraordinarily intense hard-X-ray flashes that last an estimated 300 attoseconds, a duration equivalent to a billionth of a billionth of a second. Using the European XFEL research facility, the team concentrated these flashes into an area approximately 100,000 times smaller than the cross-section of a typical human hair. This concentration of energy creates an exceptionally powerful beam that may allow scientists to observe and potentially control the rapid movements of electrons during chemical reactions and within atoms and molecules. The experiment was conducted in April 2026, and the findings were published in the journal Optica. Ichiro Inoue from the University of Tokyo, the publication's first author, stated the achievement is a world record in both intensity and fluence for a hard-X-ray attosecond pulse. Hard X-rays are a form of light characterized by extremely short wavelengths. To measure the power of these pulses, scientists use fluence, which is the amount of energy delivered to a specific area, and intensity, which accounts for how quickly that energy is delivered. To achieve this level of concentration, the team utilized a specialized optical arrangement known as an advanced Kirkpatrick-Baez (AKB) system.
